rows.state_machine: CallSession direction/state/media capability -> active-call or TranscriptEntry presentation -> scale-specific icon; icon bytes own no call transition.

rows.failure_cases: incoming/outgoing direction mismatch; voice/video affordance mismatch; inaccessible active state; asset used as call truth
rows.ui_disposition: Reuse existing HumanCallControls plus canonical TranscriptEntry/Status/IconButton; preserve a11y labels and state-derived styling with Fabushi-neutral assets.

rows.fabushi_target: Unified source-neutral two-party/group/video CallSession surface and transcript call entry. Group-call, recording, rating, participant/media controls extend the same CallSession architecture rather than a Telegram call runtime.

rows.failure_cases: two-party owner falsely treated as group-call complete; group call history misrepresented; rating feedback discarded or coupled to transport state

rows.side_effects: Actions may mutate participant membership, mute, pin, share, device/media or raised-hand state; mutations must route through the single canonical call domain.
rows.failure_cases: two-party call falsely accepted as group-call parity; duplicate participant/media owner; stale mute/speaker state; recording/share/pin state divergence.
rows.ui_disposition: Extend canonical HumanCallControls/CallSession and canonical ListRow/ParticipantRow/IconButton/Status. Never introduce TelegramGroupCall state/UI roots.
rows.fabushi_canonical_owner: Canonical CallSession + call-history TranscriptEntry + participant/media/recording owners; shared Button/Icon/Status controls only project canonical state.
rows.platform_differences: Telegram raster/SVG/Lottie asset packaging and Qt style compilation are not Fabushi target architecture. Preserve responsibility/state/a11y through canonical React/Electron components and Host/server owners, not Telegram pixels.
rows.fabushi_target: Unified source-neutral two-party/group/video CallSession surface and transcript call entry. Group-call, recording, rating, participant/media controls extend the same CallSession architecture rather than a Telegram call runtime.
rows.production_evidence: Inventory exact-read and style/code attribution identifies this resource as CallSession/call-history/group-call/media-control presentation. The resource itself does not own call signaling/session truth; any missing group/recording/rating behavior remains mapped-open.
rows.test_evidence: Call lifecycle/connect/reconnect/end, participant/media state, mic/camera/screen-share, group-call membership/raised-hand/pin/volume, recording consent/finalization, post-call rating, permission/retry, keyboard/a11y/DPI and packaged real-media E2E remain required as applicable.
